Article Title: Switch to cleaner fuel: Study calls for tech-neutral stance
Article Text:
Switch to cleaner fuel

NEW DELHI: Delhi has the strongest CNG infrastructure among the cities assessed in a TERI study and, along with Bengaluru, also has relatively strong EV infrastructure.The study, supported by the Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB), found that effective charging capacity was considerably lower in Lucknow, Guwahati, Dhanbad and Chamba. It said infrastructure readiness was a key determinant of the timing of the transition and that national transition pathways needed regionally differentiated implementation strategies.The “Study on Comparative Assessment of Vehicular Fuels in India’s Energy Transition” examined petrol, diesel, CNG, electricity and LNG across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, private and commercial four-wheelers, light commercial vehicles (LCVs) and heavy-duty vehicles. It covered Delhi, Mumbai, Mumbai Port, Surat, Ahmedabad, Guwahati, Lucknow, Bengaluru, Dhanbad and Chamba.The study found that India should not adopt one fuel or technology as a universal replacement, with different technologies performing different roles across vehicle fleets, applications and stages of the transition.It found that EVs currently provide the lowest ownership costs for two-wheelers and three-wheelers, while CNG offers a relatively balanced and deployment-ready mobility solution across a wide range of personal and commercial applications.The study said CNG has a strong position in passenger cars, taxis, buses and LCVs, while LNG remains particularly relevant for long-haul freight.The study was based partly on a primary survey of 2,315 vehicle owners and drivers across 10 locations, using stratified random sampling. The survey covered vehicle usage, travel distance, mileage, infrastructure access, fuel and maintenance expenditure, technology preferences and willingness to retrofit.Economic considerations emerged as the strongest factor in the assessment, accounting for 31.49% of the overall weighting, followed by environmental considerations at 22.34% and technical factors at 21.25%. The report said the weights reflected the importance of affordability, ownership cost and operating economics in technology selection.The study said CNG-powered vehicles have the lowest overall life-cycle emissions among the fuel options assessed for several passenger and commercial vehicle segments. It also said environmental performance cannot be judged solely through tailpipe emissions, with EV performance influenced by electricity generation, battery manufacturing and material requirements.The findings come amid a continuing debate over the role of vehicles and fuels in Delhi-NCR’s air pollution and the effectiveness of past interventions. Tarun Kapoor, advisor to PM, said better data was needed to guide policy. “Good authentic data is very urgently needed. Whatever interventions we’ve done in the past, it’s been like hitting in the dark and the results have not really been the way it was thought,” he said.The study also said electrification changes rather than eliminates energy-security risks by shifting some dependence from petroleum towards electricity infrastructure, critical minerals, imported automobile components and battery supply chains.“The real policy question is not which fuel should replace all others, but rather which fuel is best suited for which application, under what operating conditions and at what stage of India’s transition journey,” said AK Tiwari, member, PNGRB.The study recommended a technology-neutral framework at the national level, with differentiated approaches based on vehicle segment, region and application. It also called for accelerated CNG infrastructure development, greater use of CBG and differentiated CNG and LNG strategies, with LNG focused on long-haul mobility.
Article Summary: Delhi has the strongest CNG infrastructure among the cities assessed in a TERI study. Bengaluru also has relatively strong EV infrastructure. Study found that effective charging capacity was considerably lower in Lucknow, Guwahati, Dhanbad and Chamba.

Article Title: LPG price hike: 19-kg commercial cylinder gets Rs 62.50 costlier; new Aadhaar rule kicks in for domestic users
Article Text:
Commercial LPG gets costlier

The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1, taking the price to Rs 2,810. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137 per litre.The changes come as domestic LPG consumers face a new requirement from October 1, 2026. Those seeking to book refills at the regulated Retail Selling Price (RSP) with applicable subsidy will now need to have completed Biometric Aadhaar Authentication (BAA).The authentication requirement is aimed at ensuring that subsidised LPG reaches genuine and deserving households. Each LPG connection is linked to an Aadhaar-authenticated consumer to prevent diversion of subsidised domestic cylinders for commercial and industrial use, remove duplicate and ineligible connections, and make subsidy delivery more targeted and transparent.Consumers who have already completed BAA will not need to repeat the process and can continue booking refills as before. Those who have not completed it will be able to book a refill at the RSP with subsidy once their authentication is completed.Consumers can complete the authentication process through several channels. During refill delivery, the delivery person can carry out BAA on the spot using the OMC mobile application.The process can also be completed by visiting the LPG distributor's showroom. Consumers can alternatively complete it themselves from home through their OMC's mobile application: IndianOil ONE for Indane customers, HelloBPCL for Bharatgas customers and HP PAY for HP Gas customers.Consumers who are unwilling or unable to complete BAA can still receive LPG. They will have to register their choice through their OMC's digital channels, including the consumer web portal, mobile app, WhatsApp chatbot, IVRS or other available channels.In such cases, LPG will be supplied at the applicable market price without subsidy, in 5-kg or 10-kg cylinders, subject to local availability with the OMC.Consumers who have not yet completed BAA have been urged to do so through any of the available channels, which are accessible in both urban and rural areas.
Article Summary: The price of a 19-kg commercial LPG cylinder has risen by Rs 62.50 from Thursday, October 1. This follows a Rs 9.50 increase in September, when the cylinder was priced at Rs 2,747.50. ATF prices have also gone up by around Rs 16 per litre, from Rs 121 to Rs 137.

LUCKNOW: Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is Samajwadi Party's 'surprise' candidate for the Rajya Sabha polls along with party's secretary general Prof Ram Gopal Yadav. Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is the Group President of Reliance Industries and considered to be very close to the Ambani family. He is also a sports administrator. The two will file their nomination papers in the presence of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav at 11 am.Recently, Akhilesh Yadav, while responding to a media query on probable candidates for Rajya Sabha had said that this time there will be a surprise candidate from SP. On Wednesday morning the party declared Nathwani's name as the second confirmed candidate of the party on SP's official X account.A founding member of SP and party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav's chief political strategist, Ram Gopal Yadav has been in the Rajya Sabha continuously since 2004. He has stood with Akhilesh through all the thick and thin and sided with him during the battle for supremacy within the Yadav clan in the run-up to 2017 assembly polls.As per the math in place, SP has INDIA bloc MLAs to see through two of its candidates in Rajya Sabha and will need some outside MLAs for any third candidate.As Group President at Reliance Industries Limited (RIL), Dhanraj looks after Corporate Affairs, Finance, HR, and CSR. He oversees the operations of Reliance's Jamnagar and Vadodara manufacturing divisions in Gujarat.Dhanraj is also a Director in other Reliance Group entities including Reliance New Energy Limited.He was unanimously elected as the President of Gujarat Cricket Association (GCA) in 2022 succeeding Union Home Minister Amit Shah and also is also the President of Gujarat State Football Association.Dhanraj also happens to be the Vice-President of the administrative committee of the famous Dwarkadhis Temple and has directed the famous mega-musical show 'Rajadhiraj: Love.' based on the life journey of Lord Krishna.With a Bachelor's Degree in International Business from Regent Business School (London), Dhanraj is an animal lover actively involved in wildlife conservation. He has been associated with campaigns for conservation of Gir lions.

Article Title: 'Had productive conversation': PM Modi speaks with US President Trump on trade, defence, energy

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday said that he had a "productive conversation" with US President Donald Trump and reviewed bilateral cooperation between New Delhi and Washington in various sectors.In a social media post on X, PM Modi said the leaders agreed to maintain close engagement to take their Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward."Had a productive conversation with President Trump. We reviewed our bilateral cooperation in trade, defence, energy, critical technologies and other areas. We agreed to maintain close engagement to take our Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership forward," PM Modi said."We also exchanged views on regional and international issues, including ongoing efforts to advance global peace and security," he added.The two leaders agreed to remain in touch as both sides continue to deepen the strategic partnership.This comes days after Trump signed into law a sweeping sanctions package targeting Russia and Iran and giving his administration expanded powers to penalise countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, including India.The legislation is particularly significant for India because it gives Trump the authority to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from the five largest buyers of Russian oil or natural gas.India and China are among the major purchasers of Russian crude.Earlier in September, the ministry of external affairs warned the US of the legislation's potential impact on the US-India relationship."This issue has been discussed at high levels in recent months with various US interlocutors. Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side," the ministry had said.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea by the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction seeking permission to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts, declining to interfere with a Calcutta High Court order that had rejected the request.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that the Election Commission has frozen the party symbol and that the larger question of who is entitled to the funds in the accounts remains pending adjudication."We refrain from going into the merits. We are not inclined to exercise our jurisdiction under Article 136. We request high court to expedite the hearing," the bench said.The TMC had sought permission to operate four accounts with public sector banks that were debit-frozen by the West Bengal Police, arguing that the FIRs related to the freeze contained procedural lapses.Separately, the Enforcement Directorate (ED) has frozen Rs 440 crore in three accounts held by the party with HDFC Bank as part of its investigation into the alleged laundering of Rs 160 crore in party funds through Kolkata-based Carewell Aviation.The agency alleges that the funds were used to purchase an Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft and an Agusta helicopter for Rs 112 crore through what it described as dubious transactions.The ED said the aircraft and helicopter were later rented to the TMC, with substantial amounts transferred on the pretext of their use.“The Embraer Legacy 600 aircraft and Agusta helicopter were rented to TMC itself, even though they were purchased from the corpus of the party, and substantial amounts were transferred on the pretext of aircraft usage. The above stated dubious arrangement is under probe to ascertain the actual beneficial purpose of the transactions,” the ED said.The Calcutta High Court on August 27 had refused to pass an interim order allowing the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts holding around Rs 804 crore. It had observed that granting such relief would undermine its earlier order allowing the political party to meet its day-to-day expenses.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed a plea by the Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction seeking permission to operate four debit-frozen bank accounts. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale noted that the Election Commission has frozen the party symbol and that the larger question of who is entitled to the funds remains pending adjudication.

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Thursday said the “chorus of voices” against what it called the “capture of the electoral system” was growing louder, and asserted that citizens would no longer tolerate “vote chori” in any form.Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh made the remarks while citing former chief election commissioner O P Rawat’s criticism of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition MPs are also scheduled to march to the Election Commission on October 6, while opposition leaders plan to meet the President over alleged irregularities in voter-list revision.The bloc has also demanded that future elections be conducted using ballot papers and called for the Supreme Court to expedite cases concerning SIR and alleged electoral malpractices.The controversy comes as the Election Commission continues to review several issues linked to voter registration, electoral-roll databases and its IT systems following concerns raised internally by Sandhu and Joshi.

Article Title: Supreme Court allows sale, manufacture of next-generation green firecrackers
Article Text:
Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Ahead of the festive season, Supreme Court on Wednesday paved the way for the manufacture and sale of next-generation joined green firecrackers after Centre's recommendation. Commonly known as 'ladi', these were earlier banned by the court.SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that while the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned, the activity would not be allowed at all hours.Additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale that government had recommended that joined firecrackers, which complied with norms fixed by Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI), be allowed. The issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15.Submitting the findings of CSIR-NEERI, Bhati said the report said 25 braids were burst in one second in conventional joined firecrackers whereas in next-generation joined firecrackers, only five braids were burst in a second.Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority as well as with the prescribed noise limit and emission and safety requirements fixed under the law.Advocate Pranav Sachdeva, appearing for some manufacturers, assured the bench they would do so.As the pollution crisis in winter has become an annual affair in Delhi, the bench said it would pass a separate order for the national capital. "We're making this very clear. Neither are we going to agree with you for a total ban nor are we going to allow it 24 hours," the court said.A total ban would have a "sentimental effect", SC said, but allowing bursting of crackers throughout the day would have a "huge impact on every other living being, including old people, sick people and children"."We need to find a solution whereby we can give specified time and we can specify what crackers are to be used," the bench told the petitioner seeking curbs on the sale of firecrackers in NCR.Earlier, two government organisations had taken contradictory stands in SC on allowing next-generation green firecrackers. While CSIR-NEERI approved them saying their pollution levels had decreased by 40-60% and recommended commercial production of flowerpots, sparklers, 'chakkars', pencils, 'ladis' and twinkling stars, Central Pollution Control Board said they contained barium nitrate, which was banned by SC.
Article Summary: Government said manufacturers must comply with specifications/formulations tested and approved by the competent authority. Issue of using barium chemical remains undecided as the ASG told the bench that field trials were on, and sought time till Oct 15. SC also said a separate order would be passed for Delhi and indicated that the bursting of firecrackers would not be banned at all hours.

Article Title: Second full EC meet in 5 days, SIR extended again in Andhra Pradesh, Meghalaya
Article Text:
Chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar with election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi

NEW DELHI: The full Election Commission - comprising CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - met Wednesday, a second time in five days, and decided to extend the deadlines for the ongoing SIR exercise in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya, reports Bharti Jain.The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in Andhra will now run from July 31 to Oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to Oct 16. For Meghalaya, the date for publication of the final poll roll has been revised to Oct 26.The second full meeting of the commission since an Indian Express report alleged that ECs Sandhu and Joshi had objected to steps taken by EC on 14 occasions over 10 months reaffirms that the CEC and the two ECs have agreed to sit together and transact normal business of the commission through regular meetings.The draft roll of Meghalaya published on Aug 5 listed 21.7 lakh electors, with around 7.7% absent, shifted, dead and duplicate electors deleted. In Andhra, the draft roll listed 3.7 crore electors after deleting 10.8% of its electorate.
Article Summary: The full Election Commission - comprising CEC Gyanesh Kumar and ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi - met Wednesday, a second time in five days. The revised period for disposal of claims and objections in Andhra will now run from July 31 to Oct 10. The date for publication of the final poll roll also stands extended to Oct 16.

Article Title: Panel eyes 'debundling' of exam responsibilities
Article Text:
Separating the functions could limit concentration of control over the process. The panel is also planning a common calendar involving NTA, SSC, IBPS and RRBs.

Test facilities to move closer to candidates

NEW DELHI: Question-paper setting, exam conduct, test centres and security will be handled by separate agencies under a restructuring being prioritised by the Nandan Nilekani-led task force on exam reforms. This "debundling" of responsibilities is central to a plan that also envisages exam centres in every district and a common calendar for major testing bodies.Separating the functions could limit concentration of control over the process. The panel is also planning a common calendar involving NTA , SSC, IBPS and RRBs.A common calendar for major testing bodies — NTA, SSC, Institute of Banking Personnel Selection and Railway Recruitment Boards — could help bring in coordinated scheduling to reduce clashes. It could further allow better use of exam infrastructure throughout the year.Centres in every district would bring testing facilities closer to candidates, particularly those in rural areas. The plan comes as the education ministry develops a national computer-based testing infrastructure strategy to support the migration of pen-and-paper entrance examinations, including NEET-UG.According to a govt official, the strategy aims to close geographic gaps in test-centre availability and establish uniform standards for examination facilities.Ashish Mittal, managing director of examination security provider Innovatiview, said: “The focus must be on ensuring that technology, physical infrastructure, security and operations integrate into one auditable examination system with candidate experience at the epicentre.”
Article Summary: Question-paper setting, exam conduct, test centres and security will be handled by separate agencies. Separating the functions could limit concentration of control over the process. The panel is also planning a common calendar involving NTA, SSC, IBPS and RRBs. Test facilities to move closer to candidates.

The project will support regional integration, trade and commerce, tourism and logistics, while contributing to sustained socio-economic development across the region.”He added that improved road infrastructure and enhanced connectivity will help reduce travel time, ease congestion and improve the efficiency of movement of goods and services, benefiting local communities, businesses and the wider regional economy.Earlier this week, Gadkari had announced a decision to build a 630-km corridor connecting Siliguri in West Bengal with Guwahati (Assam) and Shillong (Meghalaya), at a cost of Rs 61,500 crore. The road transport ministry has also taken up an expressway connectivity project from Gorakhpur (UP) to Siliguri.Once completed, the two corridors will provide high-speed connectivity between UP and the North East.

Article Title: Cabinet clears Rs 1,789cr intelligent traffic system for Delhi, first planned before 2010 CWG
Article Text:
Cabinet approves Intelligent Traffic Management System for Delhi

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for Delhi to get a smart, technology-driven traffic management system over the next couple of years, the Union Cabinet on Wednesday approved the implementation of ITMS at an estimated cost of Rs 1,789 crore. The project to be implemented by Delhi police will feature AI-enabled signals, real-time congestion detection, automated enforcement and priority movement for ambulances across 42 key corridors.The proposal for an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) was first initiated ahead of the 2010 Commonwealth Games, though now the scale has been expanded to use the latest technology to detect nearly 20 types of violations and cover more stretches.Announcing the decision, Union I&B minister Ashwini Vaihnaw said the project will add “brain” to Delhi’s traffic management system as it will make the city’s traffic management infrastructure “intelligent” by integrating existing traffic signals, CCTVs, and AI capabilities into a unified, centralised control system.PM Narendra Modi , in a post on X, said the decision will “ensure the usage of technology to boost ‘Ease of Living’ across Delhi.”The project will be implemented in three phases over two years, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.On the need for the project, Vaishnaw said that at present, Delhi’s 1,529 traffic signals run on fixed timings with manual interventions and these can’t adjust on their own when traffic builds up at a junction. He added that the cameras installed to detect red-light jumping and speeding work in isolation as “there is no single city-wide system that links signal control, enforcement, traffic information and diversions or that uses AI to flag wanted vehicles”.He added that the ITMS brings signal control, enforcement and live traffic information onto one technology platform. Govt said under this new regime, adaptive signals will be synced across corridors and congestion can be spotted early. The AI-enabled system will detect violations and can flag stolen or hot-listed vehicles as well.In an official statement, govt said the system will enable traffic signals to automatically adjust timings based on prevailing road conditions and coordinate signals along identified corridors to reduce stoppages and delays. It will also facilitate priority movement of ambulances and other emergency vehicles through green corridors, besides enabling quicker detection of congestion, slow-moving traffic and road incidents, allowing police to take faster operational measures.It said variable message signs and digital platforms will provide commuters with information on congestion, diversions, parking availability and traffic conditions. Such information may also be shared with navigation service providers.The system will strengthen automated enforcement against violations such as red-light and stop-line violations, speeding, wrong-way driving, non-use of helmets and seat belts, illegal parking and use of mobile phones while driving. AI-based analytics will also assist in identifying repeat violators and vehicles linked to hit-and-run incidents.Officials said the system will have multiple layers. The physical layer includes data centres, networks, controllers, sensors, and enforcement cameras that can read vehicle number plates automatically. The digital layer will integrate devices for real-time data capture and processing, while the application layer will cover traffic analytics, enforcement, parking, congestion and signal control, incident management, video systems, and adaptive traffic control.The system will also assist police in handling vehicle breakdowns, debris on roads, accident detection, monitoring VVIP movements, and managing route diversions. During emergencies, it will also help ensure smooth and priority movement of ambulances and disaster response vehicles by monitoring and clearing routes, officials added.P K Sikdar, a former director of Central Road Research Institute (CRRI), said the decision will provide additional smartness to the city’s traffic."However, the smart city infrastructure and all these additional features need to be developed to an integrated platform with matured participation from all executive agencies of the city involved directly and indirectly in the transport system of the city," he added.Sikdar said this integrated platform should serve enforcement against all types of violations to incident detection and emergency response, and also for the alerts to the road users. "Most importantly, the public transport system is required to be highly modernised to change the preference of the public for the personalized modes. This is the opportunity to change the future direction of the city; but that is likely to demand significantly more resources," he said.
Article Summary: The proposal for an Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS) was first initiated ahead of the 2010 Commonwealth Games. The project to be implemented by Delhi police will feature AI-enabled signals, real-time congestion detection, automated enforcement and priority movement for ambulances across 42 key corridors.

The inspections will be carried out by specialised teams led by 39 experienced and retired engineers from various govt organisations, including from road transport, railways and defence ministries and from state PWDs. Article Title: 'No ban but also not 24x7': SC on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR ahead of Diwali

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday said it would not impose a blanket ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, but would also not permit fireworks throughout the day, saying a balance had to be struck between public health concerns and people’s sentiments.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale said the court would consider allowing firecrackers only during specified hours."We will make it very clear. Neither we are going to agree for total ban, nor are we going to allow them to do it (fireworks) for 24 hours a day. Total ban will affect sentiments. And allowing them throughout the day will have huge impact on every other living being including the old, sick and children," the bench orally observed, as quoted by PTI."We need to find a solution by which we can give a specified time," it added.The observations came during a hearing in which the Centre proposed a limited relaxation for a category of next-generation joined green crackers developed with technical inputs from the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI).Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati submitted a note saying the court could consider permitting the specified green crackers subject to conditions on their manufacture, chemical composition, noise levels and emissions.According to the note, only duly licensed manufacturers would be allowed to produce the crackers. They would also have to meet the prescribed noise limit of 125 dB(AI)/145 dB(C) peak and could not contain banned chemicals.The proposed crackers are linked or joined fireworks formulated with reduced quantities of barium salts, with the aim of lowering emissions. The proposal is based on the category recommended by CSIR-NEERI and would be subject to applicable safety, noise and emission standards.The bench further said it would consider the issue concerning the use of barium in firecrackers on October 15.The court's latest observations come ahead of Diwali and follow its earlier orders regulating the manufacture, sale and use of firecrackers in Delhi and the National Capital Region.Last year, the Supreme Court allowed the sale and use of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR subject to conditions, including restrictions on when they could be used.The court had said their use would be limited to specified hours on the days before Diwali and on Diwali itself, as part of measures aimed at balancing festival-related celebrations with concerns over air pollution and public health.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says it will not impose blanket ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR. Justices say balance has to be struck between public health concerns and people's sentiments. Centre proposes limited relaxation for a category of next- generation joined green crackers.

Article Title: ‘Dangerous path’: MEA urges Indians to stay away from Russian military recruitment

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs has issued a fresh advisory cautioning Indians against joining the Russian armed forces, warning of the “mortal dangers” involved and urging citizens to exercise due diligence when considering job offers in Russia.The advisory, issued on Wednesday, comes amid continued reports of Indian nationals being recruited into the Russian military.The government said it has repeatedly highlighted the risks involved and urged Indians not to be lured by unverified employment offers.The MEA said some Indian nationals have willingly sought offers to advising Indian nationals to refrain from taking such actions.The government also cautioned Indians about recruitment by non-public entities, including voluntary groups, saying foreign nationals were being recruited to serve in the Russian armed forces through such organisations.The MEA advised Indians to exercise due diligence before accepting job offers from agents that are not registered with the ministry of external affairs.The government said it remains engaged with Russia to ensure the safety, well-being and early discharge of all Indian nationals serving in the country's armed Article Title: India's monsoon rainfall ends 13% below normal, fourth-lowest since 2001
Article Text:
File photo: People and Children enjoy the rain near India Gate during a monsoon shower, in New Delhi (Picture credit: ANI)

El Niño weighs on monsoon rainfall

Late rains narrowed the deficit

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India received 87.4 per cent of its long period average (LPA) rainfall during the June-September southwest monsoon this year, making it the fourth-lowest monsoon rainfall recorded since 2001, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).The country received 759.4 mm of rainfall against the normal seasonal average of 868.6 mm, leaving a deficit of about 13 per cent between June 1 and September 30, the IMD said on Wednesday.The season's rainfall was marked by an uneven distribution across different parts of the country, with several regions recording significant deficits despite heavy rain spells towards the end of the monsoon.A senior IMD official told Reuters that India recorded 12.6 per cent below-average rainfall during the June-September season, with the El Niño weather pattern contributing to weaker precipitation.India is likely to receive below-average rainfall in October, while most parts of the country are expected to record below-normal rainfall during the October-December period, according to the weather office.The IMD's LPA refers to the average rainfall recorded over a particular region during a specified period, calculated over a long-term period, typically spanning 30 to 50 years.The 2026 monsoon is the first deficient season since 2015. The IMD classifies seasonal rainfall that is 10 per cent or more below the LPA as deficient.The monsoon began with a rapid advance after reaching Kerala on June 4, three days later than its normal arrival date, but subsequently stalled for nearly two weeks before reaching northwest India in the first week of July.June ended with a countrywide rainfall deficit of more than 35 per cent, the highest in 12 years.Rainfall activity picked up in the following months, with several low-pressure systems forming over the Bay of Bengal and moving inland. Four such systems formed in July, six in August and three in September, including a deep depression that crossed the north Andhra-south Odisha coast on September 23-24.These systems helped bring substantial rainfall to parts of central and eastern India, narrowing the overall seasonal deficit.The impact, however, varied significantly across regions. Odisha recorded its wettest monsoon in 20 years, while the East and Northeast region was heading towards its driest monsoon since records began in 1901.South India recorded a rainfall deficit exceeding 23 per cent, making it the region's driest southwest monsoon since 2002. West Rajasthan recorded a 31 per cent deficit, while Punjab's rainfall was 42 per cent below normal.The IMD's final assessment comes after a late-season spell of heavy rainfall reduced the country's overall deficit, but the June-September season still ended well below its long-term average.
Article Summary: India received 87.4 per cent of its long period average (LPA) rainfall during the June-September southwest monsoon. The country received 759.4 mm of rainfall against the normal seasonal average of 868.6 mm, leaving a deficit of about 13 per cent. The 2026 monsoon is the first deficient season since 2015.

Article Title: Upanishads to Mahabharata: NCERT explains roots of national, SC mottos
Article Text:
The NCERT has introduced a groundbreaking Class IX social science textbook that bridges modern principles of governance with ancient Indian wisdom.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: NCERT’s new Class IX social science textbook traces India’s national motto, “Satyameva Jayate”, to the Mundaka Upanishad and the Supreme Court’s “Yato Dharmastato Jayah” to the Mahabharata, linking modern institutions to ancient texts. The lesson presents these connections as expressions of the values and responsibilities that should guide governance in a democracy.“Understanding Society: India and Beyond”, Part 2, became available on Tuesday, September 29, nearly six months into the academic session. Part 1 came out in June. The six-chapter volume, which TOI reported on Wednesday, spans history, geography, political science and economics under the National Education Policy 2020 and National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023.The chapter “Governance and Public Policy” translates the national motto as “Truth alone triumphs” and the Supreme Court’s motto as “Where there is Dharma (righteous duty), there is victory”. It places these alongside the Sengol and Gandhi’s conception of Ram Rajya.These references are “not just symbolic or superficial”, the book says, but express institutional values and the responsibility to ensure good governance.It contrasts the national motto with “Heaven’s Light, Our Guide”, used by the British Order of the Star of India. The chapter acknowledges that colonial institutions persisted after Independence, but says India’s leaders framed the Constitution in keeping with India’s own values and ideals.The Sengol is described as a “cultural marker of rulership and good governance”, with a tradition dating back more than 1,000 years to the Cholas. Prime Minister Narendra Modi installed it near the Lok Sabha Speaker’s chair in the new Parliament building on May 28, 2023.The textbook recounts Jawaharlal Nehru receiving the sceptre from Tamil Nadu’s Adheenam saints at Independence. Modi had described it as a symbol of the transfer of power. Congress disputed this in 2023, saying there was no documentary evidence that Mountbatten, C Rajagopalachari or Nehru had described it in those terms.Gandhi’s Ram Rajya is presented as an ideal rooted in probity, transparency, compassion and welfare. The chapter links it to the Ramayana and 16th-century Ramcharitmanas, calling it “one of the best examples of good governance and a good collective life”. It discusses Rajdharma as the ruler’s duty to protect people and uphold righteousness.“Good governance was measured not only by the ruler’s authority but by the peace, prosperity, justice, and well-being in society,” it says. The chapter also draws on Kautilya’s Arthashastra to place the ruler’s happiness in the happiness of the people.The chapter also identifies seven features of good governance: responsiveness, transparency, participation, rule of law, accountability, effectiveness and inclusiveness.It stresses citizens’ rights, equality before the law and access to public services, while assigning responsibilities to government, citizens, the media, civil society and the private sector in achieving public welfare.
Article Summary: “Understanding Society: India and Beyond”, Part 2, became available on Tuesday, September 29, nearly six months into the academic session. It spans history, geography, political science and economics under the National Education Policy 2020 and National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023. The chapter “Governance and Public Policy” translates the national motto as “Truth alone triumphs’.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.

Vegetables are getting more expensive by the day, with onion prices soaring 48.27% in August. Items such as air conditioners, TVs and refrigerators are also set to become more expensive. Household savings are steadily declining, while family debt is mounting. In such a scenario, how is the common family supposed to meet its needs?” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote on X.Ramesh questioned why PM Modi continues to “sermonise” in the Mann Ki Baat series instead of addressing the public’s concerns.“In his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ radio series, the Prime Minister keeps sermonising on various issues, but when will he address the country’s most pressing concern—inflation? When will he care about the public’s worries? The public is already beleaguered by rising prices, and there’s no relief coming from the government.How on earth is the average family supposed to manage its budget? How long will the middle class and the poor have their backs broken like this?” the Rajya Sabha MP asked.According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s (MoSPI) Consumer Price Index (CPI) release, retail inflation, based on the 2024=100 CPI, stood at 4.82% in August, up from 4.45% in July. Food inflation, measured by the Consumer Food Price Index (CFPI), rose to 5.95% in August from 5.52% in July. The August figures are provisional.Official data showed that onion inflation surged from 22.54% in July to 48.27% in August. Ginger recorded inflation of 73.82%, while garlic inflation stood at 43.60%. In contrast, tomato prices fell 31.09% year-on-year, while potato prices declined 13.14%.MoSPI data showed inflation in the combined food and beverages category at 5.66% in August. Transport inflation stood at 4.60 percent, education services at 3.73%, while restaurants and accommodation services recorded inflation of 8.38%. Personal care, social protection and miscellaneous goods and services registered inflation of 15.17%.The CPI data was compiled from price information collected across 1,407 urban markets, including online markets, and 1,465 villages nationwide. MoSPI reported a 100% response rate from both rural and urban markets in August.According to MoSPI, the next CPI data, covering September, is scheduled to be released on October 12.
Article Summary: The opposition party’s attack came a day after PM Modi addressed the nation in the 138th episode of Mann Ki Baat. “The brunt of inflation is no longer confined just to the kitchen, yet the Prime Minister remains blissfully unconcerned, beating his drum away,” Congress MP Jairam Ramesh wrote.

Article Title: Lung cancer deaths down 16% with low-dose CT screening: IARC
Article Text:
Lung cancer deaths can be reduced through low-dose CT screening, which can also help detect the disease before it reaches advanced stages in people at high risk, according to an IARC assessment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people, while also reducing the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, an International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) working group has found.Published in The New England Journal of Medicine, the assessment found established evidence that low-dose CT reduces lung cancer mortality when used in people at high risk based mainly on age and smoking history.IARC convened a working group of 23 clinicians and scientists from 17 countries, including Dr Abhishek Shankar of All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, to assess the benefits and harms of lung cancer screening.The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history, typically at least 20 to 30 pack-years. Studies involving former smokers generally included those who had quit within the previous 10 to 15 years, with screening usually performed annually.In India, people aged 50 to 80 with at least 20 pack-years of smoking who are current smokers or quit within the past 15 years can contact the Indian Lung Screening Trial, led by Dr Abhishek Shankar at AIIMS, New Delhi, about screening.Dr Shankar has invited eligible people to contact him for screening under the trial.The evidence behind the finding came mainly from randomised trials. In the US National Lung Screening Trial, people screened with low-dose CT had a 16% lower relative risk of dying from lung cancer than those screened with chest X-rays at seven years. The European NELSON trial also found lower lung cancer mortality among men screened with low-dose CT at 10 years.Based on this evidence, the IARC group classified low-dose CT as Group A, indicating established evidence that it reduces lung cancer mortality and the incidence of stage III or IV disease. Chest X-rays, with or without sputum examination, were classified as Group C, as their ability to reduce lung cancer mortality could not be established.However, the review cautioned that low-dose CT screening is not meant for everyone. False-positive results ranged from 1% to 42% across studies, depending on the screening protocol. Among those with false-positive results, 5% to 32% underwent at least one invasive procedure, with complications occurring in 10% to 22% of such procedures.The review also estimated that 3% to 26% of lung cancers detected in randomised trials involving high-risk people could represent overdiagnosis, meaning cancers that might not have caused harm during the person's lifetime.The working group said effective lung cancer screening needs more than CT scanners, including systems for identifying eligible people, assessing risk, monitoring nodules, providing treatment and follow-up, along with smoking-cessation support. Organised programmes also require trained staff, quality assurance, adequate healthcare capacity and equitable access.
Article Summary: Low-dose computed tomography (CT) screening can cut the risk of dying from lung cancer by 16% in high-risk people. It can also reduce the incidence of advanced stage III or IV disease, according to an IARC assessment. The evidence mainly applies to people aged 50 to 80 with a substantial smoking history.

Article Title: Travis Kelce's $200 million Six Flags investment faces new low as investors push for a potential sale
Article Text:
Travis Kelce (Getty Images)

Six Flags faces mounting financial pressure

Travis Kelce’s Six Flags investment faces another test

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Six Flags is facing a fresh challenge after an investor group that includes Travis Kelce pushed the theme park company to consider a possible sale. The move comes as the operator deals with heavier losses, fewer visitors and pressure on its stock price. Jana Partners, which joined Kelce and other investors in taking a stake in Six Flags, is now seeking action from the company’s board. The development marks a sharp turn from the group’s earlier effort to help strengthen the parks and improve their appeal to families.Jana Partners reportedly contacted Six Flags’ board on Tuesday and asked it to bring in an investment bank to examine a potential sale. The request followed disappointment over the company’s latest financial results, which showed how difficult the current environment has become for the theme park operator.Six Flags posted a $203 million net loss for the second quarter, more than double the $100 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier. Attendance also fell. The company reported 13.1 million guest visits, down about 7% from 14.2 million visits in the comparable period.The pressure has also reached the stock market. Six Flags shares traded at about $12.43 on Wednesday, roughly half their yearly peak of close to $25.Jana Partners and fellow investors, including Kelce, acquired a combined stake of around 9% in Six Flags last October. Their investment was valued at roughly $200 million at the time. Jana had previously focused on improving the company's marketing and customer experience while also considering strategic options that could increase shareholder value.Six Flags said it remains focused on its investors and its wider business plans."We have a history of engaging constructively with all of our shareholders and value their perspectives. We are focused on executing on our strategic priorities and are committed to maximizing shareholder value."Kelce's connection to Six Flags goes beyond his investment. The Kansas City Chiefs star has long had an attachment to Cedar Point in Ohio, a park he visited while growing up.When the investment was announced, Kelce shared his excitement about helping shape the company's future."Couldn't pass up the opportunity to continue the tradition and make Cedar Point and Six Flags even more special for the next generation of families!"He added, "Excited to partner with JANA Partners as an investor in Six Flags. So crazy to even imagine this is real, but you gotta love it when life comes full circle."The company is also dealing with legal challenges involving its X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in California. Three people who say they suffered serious brain injuries after riding the attraction have filed lawsuits. The coaster, known for rotating seats and head-first drops, remains closed.Attorney Christopher Bulone said, "No ride like that should be allowed to exist," according to CNN.Six Flags declined to comment on the pending lawsuits but confirmed to KABC that the ride "remains closed at this time."
Article Summary: Six Flags posted a $203 million net loss for the second quarter, more than double the $100 million loss recorded during the same period a year earlier. Six Flags shares traded at about $12.43 on Wednesday, roughly half their yearly peak of close to $25. The company is also dealing with legal challenges involving its X2 roller coaster.

Article Title: Japan raises permanent residency fee 20-fold as foreign population hits record
Article Text:
File photo: Tourists look at Mt. Fuji, covered with its first snow of the season, from Fujikawaguchiko, Yamanashi Prefecture, in Japan

Why is Japan tightening permanent residency rules?

Japan is getting stricter as it gets more dependent

Japan has raised the fee for foreigners seeking permanent residency 20-fold, from 10,000 yen to 200,000 yen, as the government tightens the requirements for those seeking to settle in the country permanently.The new fee took effect on October 1. Applications submitted by September 30 remain subject to the old 10,000-yen charge, even if approval comes after the fee change.The steep increase is part of a broader overhaul of Japan's permanent residency system. Revised guidelines introduce stricter standards on income and pension eligibility, while a Japanese-language requirement is also being introduced. Most of the new criteria will apply to applications filed from April 2027, although the revised income standard can apply to applications submitted as early as April 2026.The changes come as Japan's foreign resident population reaches record levels. There were 4.125 million foreign residents in Japan at the end of 2025, according to the Immigration Services Agency, up from about 2.23 million a decade earlier.The government has linked the fee increases to the rising administrative burden of managing a growing foreign population. A bill enacted in May raised the statutory ceiling for permanent residency fees from 10,000 yen to 300,000 yen, allowing the government to set the actual charge at 200,000 yen.Prime minister Sanae Takaichi's government has made the management of immigration and the integration of foreign residents a policy priority, while Japan continues to rely on overseas workers amid an ageing population and labour shortages.Applicants must now demonstrate that they can support themselves financially, with the revised guidelines requiring income to continuously exceed the average for Japanese households of a comparable size.Pension requirements have also been tightened. Applicants' projected pension benefits must meet a benchmark equivalent to what a person would receive after 30 years in the employees' pension system at the relevant income level. Those whose projected benefits fall short can have savings and other assets taken into account.Japanese-language ability is another new element. The revised guidelines include Japanese proficiency among the factors considered in permanent residency screening, with most of the new requirements taking effect for applications from April 2027.The changes build on earlier tightening of the system. In February, Japan revised its permanent residency guidelines to make screening stricter for applicants with a history of unpaid taxes and social insurance or healthcare premiums, even if those payments were subsequently made.The fee increase triggered a rush at immigration offices in the days before it took effect.Tokyo's main immigration bureau was packed with foreign residents on September 28, with applicants reporting waits of up to 7½ hours as they tried to complete procedures before the new fees came into force.Those unable to submit applications before the deadline now face the new 200,000-yen fee.Some applicants who meet specific criteria can receive a reduction. Under the new system, eligible permanent residency applicants can pay 20,000 yen instead, while certain categories can qualify for fee exemptions.The country is dealing with an ageing population and labour shortages that have increased its reliance on foreign workers, even as the rapid growth in the number of foreign residents has fuelled debate over immigration and integration.Takaichi has said her government wants an "orderly inclusive society" and has backed measures aimed at helping foreign residents understand Japanese language, culture and social rules. A government working group has been examining a structured Japanese-language and social-orientation programme for foreign residents, with a trial planned for fiscal 2028.The result is a two-track approach: Japan continues to bring in foreign workers to help address demographic and labour pressures, while raising the financial, administrative and integration standards for those seeking to remain permanently.
Article Summary: The new fee took effect on October 1. Applications submitted by September 30 remain subject to the old 10,000-yen charge. The government has linked the fee increases to the rising administrative burden of managing a growing foreign population. There were 4.125 million foreign residents in Japan at the end of 2025.

Article Title: An Ohio farmer facing $1 million in medical debt hoped a solar lease would pay $540,000 a year; after officials blocked the project, he had to sell land and equipment from his sixth-generation farm
Article Text:
A medical crisis turned financial strain

Statutory bans derail renewable deals

Advocacy for property rights

Rebuilding through shared labor

An Ohio farmer facing $1 million (£750,000) in medical bills had to sell land and farm machinery from his family farm after local officials blocked a solar energy project on his property. Wayne Greier, a sixth-generation farmer in Mahoning County, Ohio, planned to lease 600 acres of his farmland to a solar development company in 2021. The deal would have paid him $540,000 a year in lease payments, giving him a vital source of money as debt threatened his livelihood. "It was our saving grace," Greier told the Associated Press. "It wasn't a scary picture that everybody likes to paint about solar and the loss of farmland." The deal fell apart after township officials put local restrictions in place under a state law, stopping the renewable energy project from moving forward. Losing the income left Greier unable to keep his full farming operation running. He was forced to sell assets to pay growing debts and satisfy creditors.Greier’s financial problems began during a serious battle with COVID-19 and other health problems. According to Farm Progress, he spent 40 days in the hospital, had seven abdominal surgeries, and built up $1 million in medical debt.When an energy developer approached him in 2021 about putting solar panels on part of his 1,000-acre property, Greier saw a chance to protect his family’s future. His land already had high-voltage power transmission lines, which made it a good place to connect a solar project to the power grid. But local opposition grew quickly as residents organized against large renewable energy projects. The opposition soon became personal. According to Farm Progress, Greier said opponents protested outside his home, spread rumors that solar panels would poison local drinking water, and targeted his children at school. "All of a sudden, this mob was created that was anti-solar," Greier said in his interview with Farm Progress. "And they surrounded my house with signs. And people were telling me to move out of the community, and I had to pull my kids out of school because the other kids were saying that we were going to ruin everybody else's drinking water, and we were going to ruin the community. It was really bad. I went through a really dark time because of that."In 2021, Ohio lawmakers passed Senate Bill 52, giving county commissioners and township authorities wider powers to create restricted areas. These rules allowed local officials to block large wind and solar projects on private farmland. Green Township trustees later voted to ban commercial solar and wind projects. Greier's developer had not completed a formal impact study with the Ohio Power Siting Board before the local ban took effect, so the project was stopped. “I was the one that was going to lose the sixth-generation farm. I was the one that couldn't provide for my family,” Greier told the Associated Press. The decision quickly created financial problems for Greier. With banks threatening foreclosure, he sold parts of his land and essential farm equipment. The equipment included a 24-row planter, tillage machinery and a deep ripper. He also returned tractors that he had been leasing.After the project collapsed, Greier became a strong advocate for farmers’ land rights across the region. He regularly shares his experience with state lawmakers, industry groups, and farming communities. He argues that landowners should be able to decide how to earn money from their own property. "After all this happened, I decided that I would advocate any way possible so that nobody has to go through what I did and to prevent this in the future," Greier told Farm Progress. Greier sees the situation as a larger fight over property rights. He believes selling energy from private land is no different from growing crops or raising livestock, especially for family farms that need financial independence. "There's families that are relying on this and looking for this," he told the Associated Press. "And it's been taken away, this opportunity."Even after losing equipment and cutting back his main grain operation, Greier remains on his historic family farmland. His father’s ashes are scattered on the property, which is one reason he has chosen to stay instead of moving. To earn a living, Greier leased his remaining acreage to another local farmer while working on the land as a paid worker. He operates heavy equipment, manages grain sales, and raises livestock, including sheep, goats, and beef cattle. The arrangement has also allowed him to work alongside his 13-year-old son, Blake, helping keep their family connection to the farm alive. "He got to follow in my footsteps, and that feels good," Greier told Farm Progress.
Article Summary: Wayne Greier, a sixth-generation farmer in Mahoning County, Ohio, planned to lease 600 acres of his farmland to a solar development company in 2021. The deal would have paid him $540,000 a year in lease payments, giving him a vital source of money as debt threatened his livelihood. Local officials put local restrictions in place under a state law, stopping the renewable energy project from moving forward. Losing the income left Greier unable to keep his full farming operation running.

Article Title: Mumbai train alert: 75-day CSMT block from October 1; 8 long-distance trains short-terminated
Article Text:
Central Railway will implement a 75-day traffic and power block at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus from October 1 (File photo)

Seven trains will be short-terminated at Dadar:

11002 Ballarshah-CSMT Nandigram Express

12810 Howrah-CSMT Express

12112 Amravati-CSMT Express

11020 Bhubaneswar-CSMT Konark Express

22120 Madgaon-CSMT Tejas Express

22144 Bidar-CSMT Express

22108 Latur-CSMT Express

12134 Mangaluru-CSMT Express will be short-terminated at Thane





MUMBAI: Central Railway will impose another 75-day traffic and power block at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) from October 1 to December 15 for the redevelopment of the heritage terminus, resulting in eight long-distance trains being short-terminated at Dadar and Thane.The block will cover platforms 14 and 15 and stabling line 15 and will be undertaken in connection with Phase-I of the CSMT redevelopment being executed by the Rail Land Development Authority (RLDA).Foundation work and other essential construction activities will be carried out during the block, with train operations from the two platforms suspended until the work is completed.The latest block comes after a prolonged closure of platforms 16 and 17 for the same redevelopment project.The earlier block began on February 1 and was initially scheduled for 85 days, till April 26. It was subsequently extended several times, with Central Railway saying the block continued until September 5.During this period, 10-14 long-distance trains were short-terminated at Dadar and Thane at different stages.The decision to take up work on platforms 14 and 15 had been a concern for Central Railway because these platforms handle another 16-18 long-distance services every day.CR had sought to have platforms 16 and 17 made fully operational before additional platforms were taken up for construction, citing the potential for further disruption to long-distance operations.The Rs 2,450-crore CSMT redevelopment project, approved by the Union cabinet in 2022, envisages transforming the terminus into an integrated transport hub while retaining the heritage character of its main Victorian Gothic building.The project includes new buildings, an elevated deck connecting platforms, improved passenger facilities and commercial spaces. The original completion deadline of March 2026 has been extended to October 2028.On completion of the current block, RLDA will hand over platforms 14 and 15 for train operations, Central Railway said.Passengers travelling on the affected trains have been advised to plan their journeys accordingly.
Article Summary: Central Railway will impose another 75-day traffic and power block at Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) from October 1 to December 15. Eight long-distance trains will be short-terminated at Dadar and Thane. The block will cover platforms 14 and 15 and stabling line 15.

Article Title: Mangaluru-Goa Vande Bharat to be extended till Bengaluru soon
Article Text:
Vande Bharat Express trial run between Yeshwanthpur and Mangaluru reaching Mangaluru Central Railway Station on Saturday.





BENGALURU: Railway ministry will soon extend Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express to Bengaluru, meeting two long-standing demands from rail users for premium train services connecting Karnataka’s capital with Mangaluru and Goa.TOI has learnt that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw wrote to two MPs from Karnataka, Brijesh Chowta and Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri, earlier this month, communicating the decision to extend the train route.Currently, 20646/20645 Mangaluru Central–Madgaon Vande Bharat Express runs six days a week, with no service Thursdays. According to its timetable, the train takes a little less than six hours to complete a single-direction journey.Proposals to operate Vande Bharat between Bengaluru and Goa were first initiated by South Western Railway (SWR), Konkan Railway Corporation Limited (KRCL) and Southern Railway (SR), in Feb. They suggested the train originate from Yeshwantpur in Bengaluru at 6:05am and reach Madgaon in Goa by 7:15pm, taking 13 hours. Currently, trains between Bengaluru and Goa take around 15 hours.Vaishnaw said the extension will make the train terminate at Yeshwantpur Junction, traversing through Kabaka Puttur and Subrahmanya Road stations.It will become the first self-propelled train to travel along the 55-km ghats section between Sakleshpur and Subrahmanya Road after it was electrified in late 2025.Though the proposal initially suggested a bypass without entering Mangaluru Central station, the plan has now been changed. For Bengaluru-Mangaluru route, two trial runs using a 16-car rake were conducted in Sept, and the train took less than seven hours to complete the journey.The number of commercial stops in the final timetable will determine the total running time. While timings are yet to be finalised, the train will run with entirely new numbers, 26655/26656 in both directions. It will also be renamed Yeshwantpur-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express. The commencement date of the extended service has not been finalised; SWR officials did not comment on the matter.
Article Summary: Mangaluru-Madgaon Vande Bharat Express to be extended to Bengaluru. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw wrote to two MPs from Karnataka, Brijesh Chowta and Vishweshwar Hegde Kageri, earlier this month.

Article Title: Drive wrong, pay more: Karnataka mulls Rs 5,000 fine for repeat traffic offenders
Article Text:
The Karnataka government is considering increasing fines for traffic violations, particularly for habitual offenders (AI image)

This proposal includes escalating penalties and accumulating negative points for repeat violations.

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think is the most pressing issue concerning traffic violations in Karnataka? One-way driving Signal jumping Unauthorised parking Dangerous riding 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BENGALURU: The Karnataka govt is considering higher fines for one-way driving, wrongside driving, riding on footpaths, unauthorised parking, signal jumping and dangerous riding to up to Rs 5,000 for habitual offenders. At present, the basic fine for these offences is Rs 500.The govt is contemplating bringing changes to motor vehicle rules to impose higher penalties for several traffic violations. Officials said Rs 5,000 would be the upper ceiling for habitual offenders. “Fines will vary for first-time offenders and increase progressively for each additional offence,” one of them said.A key proposal discussed at a joint meeting of the transport and home departments on Wednesday, which was attended by transport minister Byrathi Suresh and home minister Priyank Kharge, was to deal with habitual offenders. Under the proposed system, motorists would accumulate negative points for traffic violations and could face suspension of their driving licences after crossing a specified limit.A senior transport department official said: “Multiple issues pertaining to easing congestion and increasing penalties for seven to eight offences were discussed at the meeting. Once we receive a formal proposal from the home department, further measures will be taken to bring changes to rules and hike penalties.”The govt is considering banning the production and sale of half-helmets over safety concerns for two-wheeler riders and pillion riders. Suresh said the govt will even take action against factories producing half-helmets, which are cheaper than ISI-marked helmets and are widely used by two-wheeler riders. However, they don’t provide adequate protection.The departments are working towards integrating the transport department’s Sarathi system with Bengaluru traffic police’s e-challan system. This would allow traffic personnel to verify driving licence details and access a motorist’s violation history while registering fresh offences.The govt is also looking at bringing low-speed battery-operated electric two-wheelers under a legal framework covering registration, applicability of traffic rules, wearing helmets and other requirements. Officials discussed measures to ensure these vehicles can be identified and their riders held accountable for traffic violations.Push for carpoolingTo reduce the number of private vehicles on Bengaluru roads, govt is also examining a state-level policy for carpooling and ride-sharing services. The proposal includes guidelines for app-based carpooling, park-and-ride facilities and promotion of shared transport.The meeting also discussed stricter action against modified silencers, shrill horns and high-intensity lights. Dedicated BMTC lanes are proposed to be restored on roads where Metro construction has been completed, while additional feeder services and higher bus frequencies on Outer Ring Road are being considered.
Article Summary: The Karnataka govt is considering higher fines for one-way driving, wrongside driving, riding on footpaths, unauthorised parking, signal jumping and dangerous riding. At present, the basic fine for these offences is Rs 500. Officials said Rs 5,000 would be the upper ceiling for habitual offenders.
