Article Title: A year on, Bengaluru-Mumbai superfast train promise remains on paper
Article Text:
Despite a promise made a year ago by the Railway Minister, no superfast train service exists between Bengaluru and Mumbai

TOI





BENGALURU: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters for years.On Sept 27, 2025, Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya announced through his X account that railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had assured him of a superfast train connecting the two cities. Twelve months later, however, the promised train has not started.For passengers, the situation has changed little. For over three decades, Udyan Express has remained the only daily direct service between Bengaluru and Mumbai that takes roughly 24 hours to cover the journey.There was some movement in May 2026, when railways introduced a bi-weekly SMVT Bengaluru-Lokmanya Tilak Terminus Express. But the additional service did not address the central demand for a faster connection: that train too takes around 24 hours.The next assurance raised expectations further. In May, Vaishnaw tolda Vande Bharat sleeper service on Bengaluru-Mumbai route will be introduced in Aug. That, too, has not materialised.The railway board subsequently allocated a rake that had initially been planned for Bengaluru-Mumbai route to Northern Railway zone, leaving passengers without a launch date for the proposed service.Rail users from across Karnataka have taken to social media to question the delay. Karnataka Rail Users sarcastically marked the first anniversary of the announcement, while other passenger groups accused the Centre and South Western Railway (SWR) zone of making promises without delivering the service.Mahendra Singhi, a member of SWR’s Zonal Railway Users’ Consultative Committee in Hubballi, said the railway board should introduce a Vande Bharat on the route to provide the speed and comfort passengers have been seeking.The BJP’s Karnataka migrant outreach network has also sought an early decision. “Nearly a year has passed since the announcement, yet there has been no official communication regarding the launch date of this service. The train will significantly benefit passengers and strengthen connectivity between Bengaluru, the IT capital of India, and Mumbai, the financial capital,“ Bharat Jain, co-convener (Karnataka), BJP Rajasthani Pravasi Prakoshth, stated.
Article Summary: A year after the Centre promised a superfast train between Bengaluru and Mumbai, there is little to show on the ground. The much-awaited service remains on paper, with passengers still relying on the same limited rail options that have frustrated traders, business travellers and regular commuters.

Article Title: Bengaluru sees flooded roads, fallen trees & traffic snarls
Article Text:
According to KSNDMC, however, Bengaluru received an average of 10mm rainfall.





BENGALURU: A spell of heavy evening rain brought parts of Bengaluru to a standstill Wednesday, flooding roads, choking traffic and leaving motorists battling waterlogged stretches across several parts of the city.The downpour, accompanied by strong winds, brought down trees at multiple locations, further disrupting evening peak-hour traffic. India Meteorological Department (IMD) officials said the city received 1.6mm of rainfall until 8.30pm. “However, rain was intense in eastern parts of the city -- over 18mm,” an official said. According to KSNDMC, however, Bengaluru received an average of 10mm rainfall.The city was overcast since morning, but rain intensified towards evening, quickly turning several arterial roads, underpasses and low-lying stretches into waterlogged corridors. Peenya flyover, Hebbal Ring Road and several underpasses were among the worst affected. Water accumulated near Hebbal Ring Road, triggering long queues of vehicles.Commuters reported waterlogging near Hoodi Metro station. Varun Rao, a commuter, posted on X that there were hardly any drains between the Metro station and Hoodi circle, resulting in rainwater flowing directly onto the main road. He said pedestrians were forced to wade through ankle- to knee-deep water.Vidyashilp railway underpass in Yelahanka, Rashtrothana flyover, Choudappa Layout and Thanisandra Road were inundated, throwing traffic out of gear. A large tree was uprooted near Vijnana Nagar, bringing traffic towards Kaggadasapura to a halt. Another tree reportedly fell near Vidhya Soudha School, adding to the evening chaos. Water stagnated along the stretch from Rainbow Hospital towards Karthik Nagar, between Yelahanka BSF and Airport Road, and from Mahadevapura towards Lorry Junction, making commuting difficult.Similar scenes were reported on Vibgyor Road in Whitefield, where waterlogging left vehicles stranded and some motorists struggling to negotiate the flooded stretch. Sahakara Nagar too witnessed significant water accumulation, with clogged drains leaving roads inundated. Traffic moved slowly through several neighbourhoods, while minor jams were reported at multiple locations.
Article Summary: The downpour, accompanied by strong winds, brought down trees at multiple locations. Peenya flyover, Hebbal Ring Road and several underpasses were among the worst affected. According to KSNDMC, however, Bengaluru received an average of 10mm rainfall.

Article Title: With 35% monsoon deficit, Karnataka stares at worst drought in 150 years
Article Text:
Mysuru is the worst-affected district while rainfall is normal in Bengaluru South





MYSURU: Karnataka has recorded its worst southwest monsoon rainfall deficit in 55 years, with rainfall from June 1 to Sept 30 falling 35% below normal, according to data from Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC). The deficit is the lowest recorded since 1971, surpassing the previous low of 33% in 2002, said G Srinivasa Reddy, former director of KSNDMC.The state received just 551 mm of rainfall against the normal 852 mm during the four-month monsoon season. While rainfall improved in July and August, September saw a sharp reversal, with the state recording a 54% deficit during the month, pushing the seasonal deficit to 35%.Of the 31 revenue districts, Mysuru was the worst affected, with a 59% deficit, followed by Vijayanagara at 57%. Only Bengaluru South recorded rainfall within the normal range, with a deficit of 18%.Usually, rainfall ranging between +19% and -19% is considered to be normal.According to KSNDMC data, in June 2026, the state recorded -42% deficit rainfall, which improved to -29% in July. In Aug, due to further improvement in rainfall, the deficit fell to -23%. However, with weak monsoon in Sept, the state recorded -54% deficit rainfall during the month, bringing the deficit for the June-Sept period to -35%.Meanwhile, Mysuru is the worst-affected district in the entire state with -59% deficit rainfall. According to data, against normal rainfall of 419 mm, Mysuru received just 172 mm from June to Sept.Vijayanagara is the second worst-affected district with -57% deficit rainfall.According to KSNDMC data, among the 31 districts, only Bengaluru South recorded a normal rainfall deficit of -18%.North interior Karnataka is the worst affected with -42% deficit rainfall, followed by south interior Karnataka, which recorded -41% deficit rainfall.Malnad region, comprising the four districts of Kodagu, Shivamogga, Hassan, and Chikkamagaluru recorded -38% deficit rainfall. The coastal region recorded -28% deficit rainfall.With inflow to dams falling, live storage in the four major dams of Cauvery basin fell to 52% of gross capacity. The combined gross capacity of Kabini, Hemavati, KRS, and Harangi is currently 114.6 TMC. However, on Wednesday, the available water was just 59.1 TMC. Inflow to KRS dam stood at just 492 cusecs.According to Reddy, even though SW monsoon withdrawal has reached Gujarat, in Karnataka, it may require another 8-10 days. He added that with the Cauvery basin’s upper catchment areas witnessing drought, the reservoirs did not record any significant inflow.
Article Summary: Karnataka has recorded its worst southwest monsoon rainfall deficit in 55 years. The state received just 551 mm of rainfall against the normal 852 mm during the four-month monsoon season. Of the 31 revenue districts, Mysuru was the worst affected, with a 59% deficit.
